Understanding IATA Codes

IATA airport codes are 3-letter identifiers assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). Each code uniquely identifies a commercial airport worldwide. For example:

  • The first letter often relates to the region or country
  • Major hub airports typically have memorable codes
  • Some cities share codes across multiple airports (e.g., NYC metro has JFK, LGA, EWR)

Understanding IATA Codes in South America

IATA airport codes are 3-letter identifiers assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA). Each code uniquely identifies a commercial airport worldwide. In South America, major hub airports typically have codes that are easy to remember and often relate to the city name:

  • Major international hubs use codes like GRU, GIG, BOG, BSB
  • Regional airports have codes that reflect their local area or city
  • Some cities with multiple airports use different codes for each (e.g., codes for international vs domestic terminals)
